checks.lead: John Jay (December 23 [O.S. December 12], 1745 – May 17, 1829) was a Founding Father of the United States. He served as the first Chief Justice from 1789 to 1795 and as the second governor of New York from 1795 to 1801. Jay was a statesman and diplomat who signed the Treaty of Paris that ended the American Revolutionary War and directed U.S. foreign policy for much of the 1780s. He was also an important leader of the Federalist Party following the ratification of the U.S. Constitution in 1788.
